newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Defy warns against import duty cuts.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Defy warns against import duty cuts.

text.p: South African white goods maker Defy on Tuesday warned against the level of cheap imports flowing into the country and said it was vital local import duties are not reduced.

Defy chief executive Ross Heron said in a statement that South African import duty levels were too low and combined with high local input costs to hamstring the industry's attempts to expand internationally and could hit jobs.
"We are concerned about further reductions in the duty structures which would certainly threaten any potential for growth and thereby limit employment opportunities severely," Heron said.
"Industry still needs time to achieve world cost standards because we are essentially a developing nation that still carries many burdens associated with the past," he added.
Defy was bought in February for 179 million rand by a consortium of its own management and Firstcorp Capital as part of the unbundling of conglomerate Malbak Ltd.
Heron said the firm's objectives were to look abroad and consolidate its hold on the local market.
"Our immediate challenge is to become world class competitors in the product lines in which we participate and to strengthen our leadership position in the local market place," he said.
